description:
Volume buttons broken? Minimum too loud? Slider goes below it. Phones, tablets.
Is your Android volume still too loud even at the lowest setting, in media, ringtones, or notifications? Your phone or tablet stops at its hardware minimum. Granular Volume goes below it.

A small floating control appears above any app, with your whole volume range on one slider: normal system volume above your device's minimum line, and a quiet zone below it, six steps of 5 dB down to a full 30 dB under the hardware minimum. Drag it anywhere, tuck it to an edge, close it when done. Your position is saved.

This is a convenience utility, not hearing protection equipment. Actual loudness depends on your device and headphones, so use good judgment with volume changes.

LOWER THAN YOUR PHONE OR TABLET ALLOWS
Granular Volume is built for the quiet end: it reduces volume below the lowest step your device's hardware allows, using Android's audio engine, on phones and tablets alike. No root required. No system volume panel replacement. No ads, no account, no internet permission at all. The quiet zone is the heart of the app, and the same slider covers your normal range too.

WHEN YOUR VOLUME BUTTONS ARE BROKEN OR NOT WORKING
Volume buttons wear out, stiffen, stop responding, or sit under a case. The dial is an on-screen volume control that stands in for them. Above the line marking your device's minimum, it sets normal system volume: tap a bar or the arrows for louder and quieter, in even 5 dB steps built from your own device's volume curve. Below the line it keeps going, quieter than the phone allows. Mute leaves alarms alone, but the quiet steps lower alarms and ringtones too.

BUILT FOR TABLETS TOO
On some tablets the lowest volume is even louder than on a phone, depending on the model. Granular Volume works the same way on Android tablets, so tablet users get the same quiet floor.

A FLOATING VOLUME CONTROL, ALWAYS IN REACH
The control lives above whatever you are doing. Open any app, start any audio, and it is there when you need it. Drag it anywhere, or tuck it to an edge between uses. One tap closes it. Your last position is remembered next time.

QUICK SETTINGS TILE
Swipe down, tap once. After the first setup, turn the control on and off from the Quiet Dial tile in Quick Settings. No shortcuts to set up, no widgets to place.

MADE FOR QUIET MOMENTS
- App calls such as WhatsApp, on phones that play them through the media output, which varies by phone. Regular phone calls never do: Android carries those on a separate path that no app can lower further, so there the control gives you your phone's own steps and the quiet steps are shown dimmed
- Sensitive IEMs and high-sensitivity headphones, where even step 1 is too loud
- Tablet speakers and headphones, where on some models the minimum step is even louder than on a phone
- White noise or lullabies for a sleeping baby, kept barely audible
- Late-night listening next to a sleeping partner
- Quiet rooms, libraries, open offices, and meditation
- ASMR and relaxation audio at a comfortable level
- Hearing aids and amplified devices where minimum system volume is too strong

DESIGNED TO STAY OUT OF THE WAY
Granular Volume does not take over your volume keys: they keep working, and inside the quiet zone the dial folds their presses into its own finer scale. It does not replace your system volume panel and it does not add an equalizer suite you did not ask for. It sits quietly on top as an overlay and changes one thing: the level, from normal volume all the way below your hardware minimum.

PRIVATE, OPEN SOURCE
This F-Droid build is free and complete: every step is included, permanently, with nothing withheld and nothing to buy. On Google Play the app comes with a seven-day trial of everything, after which the control needs a one-time purchase. No ads. No tracking. No internet permission, so the app cannot connect to anything. No account, no sign in, no analytics. Open source under the GPL-3.0 license.

PERMISSIONS, EXPLAINED
- Display over other apps: required to show the floating vol
